P2E89.d: P2E89 stands for a voltage on proximity circuit B below the band the controller accepts in a state where no plug can be present. The rule for circuit A shows how this is judged: GM's Volt checks the line with the charge door closed or while driving out of Park and sets P0D58 below 4.2 V, in 2011 after 30 failures out of 50, in the 2019 tables after 240 out of 400 samples above 20 km/h, as a Type A code with MIL.
s: Message that a charging cable is connected although none is
Vehicle cannot be put into drive mode
Warning lamp, depending on manufacturer the MIL
c: Proximity line of circuit B chafed and shorted to ground
Water or dirt in inlet B bridging the contact to earth
Defective charging cable left in the inlet
Input stage in the evaluating control unit damaged

P2E8A.d: P2E8A is the opposite of P2E89: the proximity line of circuit B sits above the accepted band. Because the evaluating controller usually pulls the pin up to a reference such as 5 V, as described for Watt & Well's EVCC, an open wire or a missing earth path reads high just like a short to a supply.
s: Charging cable on inlet B is not detected
Charging does not start on that inlet
Warning lamp, depending on manufacturer the MIL
c: Broken proximity wire or unplugged connector at inlet B
Missing protective-earth path in inlet or cable
Proximity line shorted to a supply voltage

P2E8B.d: P2E8B describes a plug-detection signal on circuit B that drops out or jumps for moments, so the car sees a connector appear and vanish although nobody touched it. The consequences follow from the purpose of the line: under SAE J1772 the proximity state is what lets the vehicle stop drawing current before the plug is released and block driving off while connected, so a flickering signal can end charging for no visibl
s: Charging stops and restarts at random
Cable-connected message appears and disappears
Fault more frequent at the start or end of charging
c: Loose low-voltage connector on the proximity line
Worn proximity contact in inlet B or on the cable plug
Chafed wire with intermittent contact to ground
Moisture in the inlet after rain or washing

P2E8C.d: Charge sequence signals 1 and 2 belong to DC fast charging to CHAdeMO, used for example on the Nissan Leaf, the Mitsubishi i-MiEV and the Outlander PHEV. Signal 1 runs over connector pin 2: the station closes its switch d1 and applies 12 V to the line, which tells the car it is ready and starts the CAN dialogue.
s: DC fast charging refused or ending with an error
AC charging continues to work
Charging fault message in the cluster
c: Sequence signal 1 line shorted to a 12 V source
Moisture or debris in the DC inlet bridging pins
Faulty input stage in the evaluating control unit
Station switch d1 not opening at the end of a session

P2E8D.d: P2E8D means the vehicle finds the first CHAdeMO sequence line low while the fast charger should be driving it. Signal 1 is the opening move of a session: once the plug is detected the station closes d1 and applies 12 V, and only after that does the CAN exchange of battery limits begin.
s: DC fast charging does not start
Station reports a communication or vehicle error
AC charging unaffected
c: Sequence signal 1 line shorted to ground
Open wire or damaged pin 2 in the DC inlet
Fast charger not closing its switch d1
Faulty input stage in the evaluating control unit

P2E8E.d: P2E8E concerns the second CHAdeMO sequence line, which works differently from the first: the station closes switch d2 to tie the line to ground, completing the circuit that sequence signal 1 feeds, and only then may the vehicle close its high-voltage contactors. Before that the connector has been latched and the vehicle has given charge permission.
s: DC session stops after insulation test without current flowing
Station shows a vehicle-side error
AC charging still possible
c: Open wire or damaged pin 10 in the DC inlet
Fast charger switch d2 not closing
Sequence signal 2 line shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty input stage in the evaluating control unit

P2E8F.d: P2E8F reports the second CHAdeMO sequence line pulled low at a time it should be released. Because the station uses d2 to connect this line to ground as the very last step before the vehicle closes its contactors, and opens d2 first when the session ends, a line already at ground early, or still at ground once d2 is open, contradicts the sequence.
s: DC fast charging refused right after plugging in
Session ends with an error instead of a normal stop
AC charging unaffected
c: Sequence signal 2 line shorted to ground
Fast charger switch d2 stuck closed
Water or dirt in the DC inlet
Faulty input stage in the evaluating control unit

P2E90.d: P2E90 says the internal power supply of charger A, the rails that feed its control and gate-driver electronics, does not behave as intended. Kia uses the code: technical bulletin ELE409 (service action SA639, December 2025) covers 2025 EV6 and 2026 EV9 built between 21 February and 18 September 2025 that store P2E9092, performance or incorrect operation, and can no longer charge on Level 1 or 2; the fix is a new inte
s: No AC charging at home or on Level 2 stations
DC fast charging may still work
Charging system warning in the cluster
c: Internal supply stage of charger A or the ICCU failed
Weak 12 V feed or loose low-voltage connector at the charger

P2E91.d: P2E91 is the same verdict for charger B: one of its internally generated supply voltages is wrong, so the charger cannot run its power stages safely. Polestar uses the code on the Polestar 3, whose grid-to-high-voltage converter GHCA reports as charger B.
s: AC charging fails while DC fast charging still works
Charging time much longer or charging stops early
Charging socket light signals a fault
c: Internal supply stage of charger B failed
Loose low-voltage connector or weak 12 V feed at charger B

P2E92.d: P2E92 concerns cars with a second electrically opened charge door. Its open-request switch or sensor must be able to rouse sleeping control units, so besides its normal signal it drives a wake-up line, and P2E92 records that the two disagree.
s: Charge door B does not open on request every time
Door opens only from the screen or the other side works normally
Increased standby drain if the line keeps waking modules
c: Open or shorted wake-up wire between switch and control unit
Worn switch or sensor at door B giving mismatched signals
Water ingress or corrosion at the door B connector
Wake-up input of the control unit faulty

P2E93.d: P2E93 is the basic circuit fault of the input with which the driver asks the second charge flap to open. On cars with a flap on each side this input is usually a touch or wipe sensor on the flap itself: Porsche's Taycan and Cayenne Electric open each flap when a hand passes over a sensor area at its rear, and Porsche's WLK2 parts list calls the passenger-side flap door B.
s: Charge flap B does not react to touch or hand gesture
Flap B still opens via the central display or app
Charging flap warning in the instrument cluster
c: Touch or wipe sensor of flap B with a wrong internal resistance
Partly broken or corroded signal wire to the flap B sensor
Moisture in the connector at the flap module
Faulty input stage in the control unit reading the sensor

P2E94.d: With P2E94 the open request input of charge flap B is electrically sound, yet its behaviour cannot be right, for example a request that stays active for far too long. Audi describes exactly this pattern for the Q6 e-tron in bulletin 2076776/1: tension in the left or right flap module can deform the flap so that it sinks into the body and the button inside the module stays pressed; the flap can then no longer be opene
s: Flap B cannot be opened from outside
Opening via the display or charging menu still works
Flap B sits deeper than the surrounding body panel
c: Deformed or recessed flap B keeping the request button pressed
Sensor of flap B shifted or not seated correctly
Ice or dirt acting on the sensor area

P2E95.d: P2E95 says the request signal from charge flap B has dropped under the bottom of its permitted range. Usual reasons are a signal wire touching ground, water bridging the connector pins or an internally shorted sensor.
s: Flap B does not open on touch, or only with the manual release
Control unit may stay awake longer, raising standby drain
Charging flap warning displayed
c: Signal wire of the flap B sensor shorted to ground
Water in the flap B connector bridging the contacts
Request sensor of flap B failed short internally

P2E96.d: P2E96 is stored when the request signal of charge flap B climbs past the top of its permitted range. Contact with a 12 V supply raises it, and so does a broken sensor ground or switch path that lets a pulled-up input float.
s: Flap B never reacts to the hand or touch
Opening from the centre console or display still works
Warning that the charging flap is impaired
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to a 12 V supply
Interrupted ground or switch path at the flap B sensor
Pushed-back or loose pin in the flap module connector

P2E97.d: P2E97 points to a request signal from charge flap B that briefly vanishes or jumps, while no permanent fault can be found. A real case with the same sensor type comes from Porsche: on the Macan Electric of model years 2023 to 2025 the optional electric flaps open when a flat hand rests on the rear third, and bulletin WRP7 explains that production tolerances could make the gesture go undetected now and then; the fix r
s: Flap B opens only on some attempts
Code stored without a lasting fault in the workshop
c: Sensor on flap B not held firmly, adhesive strip loosened
Loose terminal in the flap B connector
Harness to flap B damaged by repeated movement

P2E98.d: P2E98 is the general circuit code for the sensor that reports whether charge flap B is open or shut. Mercedes-Benz documents it: in its plug-in hybrids the separate DC charging socket has its own flap, and information LI47.70-P-078563 lists P2E9873 for a supposed electrical fault of that flap's position sensor, stored in the DC charge-connection unit N116/5 and the powertrain controller, with the MIL lit and the note
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, charging and starting normal (Mercedes)
Flap B may stay shut or show a wrong status
c: Software fault in the DC charging unit reporting a false sensor fault (Mercedes)
Position sensor of flap B with a wrong internal resistance
Damaged wire or connector between sensor and control unit

P2E99.d: P2E99 means the position signal of charge flap B is within its electrical limits yet contradicts what the flap is doing, for instance closed although the flap was just opened. On cars with two flaps such an error has side effects, because the flaps lock each other: Porsche found on the 2020 Taycan that a bad sensor signal led to a wrong end-position decision, which then blocked the flap on the other side, and replace
s: Message asking to close a charging flap although both are closed
Opposite flap A locked and not operable
Charging refused
c: Position sensor or its harness giving a wrong end-position signal
Oxidation or particles in the flap actuator that houses the detection
Software misreading the flap state at start-up

P2E9A.d: P2E9A reports that the flap B position signal has fallen under its lowest valid value. A signal wire chafed against ground, water in the connector or an internally shorted sensor are the usual reasons.
s: Flap B status in the display does not change
Charging blocked or charging flap warning
c: Position signal wire of flap B shorted to ground
Water in the sensor connector at flap B

P2E9B.d: P2E9B is the high-side position fault of charge flap B: the reading lies above anything a working sensor can deliver. A signal wire touching 12 V, or a missing sensor ground, letting the input drift upwards, are typical explanations.
s: Permanent message that a charging flap is open
Charging not possible on either side
c: Position signal wire shorted to a 12 V feed
Broken ground wire of the flap B position sensor
Corroded or loose connector at the flap module

P2E9C.d: P2E9C covers a flap B position signal that flickers or drops out briefly instead of failing for good. Common sources are loose terminals, a harness bent at every flap movement, or a sensor sitting loose in its holder.
s: Flap status in the display switches without reason
Sporadic charging flap warnings or interrupted charging
c: Loose terminal in the position sensor connector
Harness to flap B strained or chafed by flap movement
Oxidation or particles in the flap actuator with integrated detection

P2E9D.d: P2E9D concerns the output that releases or drives charge flap B, not its sensors. Depending on the design this is a latch actuator or a small motor: Audi's e-tron family uses lock actuators F496 and F497 for its high-voltage charging flaps on the two sides, and Porsche's Taycan a servo motor per charge port door.
s: Flap B does not unlock or move at all
Charging only possible on the other side
Charging flap warning in the cluster
c: Flap B actuator or motor winding open or shorted
Damaged control wire or connector to the flap B actuator
Faulty output stage in the control unit

P2E9E.d: P2E9E is a function check: the control unit commands flap B to unlock and then expects the position sensor to confirm an open flap. GM's tables for the A flap of the Volt set P0CD2 when that report is missing after 5 seconds (2011) or 13 seconds (2013, only above minus 12 °C), skip the test while position or output codes are active, and use Type B.
s: Flap B pops slightly or rocks but does not open fully
Flap B moves freely by hand because the actuator is broken
Charging flap warning, charging only on the other side
c: Flap B lock actuator or motor gears broken, often after force on the flap
Flap B frozen, dirty or binding in its housing
Software sequencing error between the two flaps
Position sensor not reporting the opened flap

P2E9F.d: P2E9F is the low-voltage form of the flap B release output fault: the driver stage measures its control line close to 0 V where a higher level is expected. A control wire chafed to body ground or an actuator winding that has shorted are the usual culprits, and a protective fuse or driver shutdown can follow.
s: Flap B does not release on any request
Blown fuse for the flap circuit possible
c: Control wire of the flap B actuator shorted to ground
Shorted winding in the flap B actuator or motor

P2EA0.d: P2EA0 marks the opposite case at the flap B release output: the line sits at a high voltage while the driver stage should be pulling it down or keeping it off. Contact with a 12 V circuit does this, and on low-side switched outputs an interrupted actuator or wire gives the same reading.
s: Flap B never releases, only the manual release helps
Actuator may run warm if powered permanently
c: Control wire of the flap B actuator shorted to 12 V
Open actuator winding or broken wire on a low-side driven output
Output stage in the control unit stuck on

P2EA1.d: P2EA1 is the general electrical fault of a sixth exhaust temperature probe on bank 1, counting from the engine towards the tailpipe. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: the diesel tables that are published stop at probe 5, which GM's 2025 table 25OBDG04A places behind the particulate filter.
s: Check engine lamp on
Particulate filter regeneration delayed or blocked
Live data for probe 6 missing or jumping
c: Corroded or heat-damaged plug of the sixth probe near the exhaust
Probe lead or internal wire broken by exhaust vibration
Harness chafed or melted along the aftertreatment
Faulty input stage or temperature evaluation module

P2EA2.d: P2EA2 says the signal of the sixth bank 1 exhaust probe sits above its upper electrical limit. Which temperature that implies depends on the element.
s: Check engine lamp, often after a single trip
Probe 6 shows an impossible extreme value in live data
Filter regeneration or SCR dosing restricted
c: Open signal or ground lead, or connector not latched
Probe element burnt open after overheating or vibration
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2EA3.d: With P2EA3 the input of the sixth bank 1 exhaust probe drops below the lowest value a healthy circuit can deliver. Electrically this is nearly always a short: the signal wire touching ground or the exhaust, or an element whose insulation has broken down.
s: Check engine lamp after the second faulty trip
Probe 6 reads far too hot or far too cold depending on type
Regeneration or SCR dosing held back
c: Signal wire chafed through to ground or to the exhaust pipe
Probe with internal short after thermal or mechanical damage
Water or road salt bridging the connector pins

P2EA5.d: P2EA5 is the plausibility fault of the sixth bank 1 exhaust probe: the voltage is electrically valid, yet the temperature does not match what the exhaust is doing. California's rule 13 CCR 1968.2, section (e)(15.2.1), like §1971.1 for heavy-duty engines, asks for two-sided rationality checks and names exhaust temperature sensors that steer a catalyst temperature strategy.
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
Probe 6 stays flat or lags while other probes heat up
Regeneration interrupted or not started
c: Probe loose or pulled from its boss after exhaust work
Drifting element or soot-coated tip reacting too slowly
Neighbouring probes swapped at their connectors
Contact resistance in the connector shifting the reading

P2EA6.d: P2EA6 is the general circuit fault of the temperature sensor in the charge pipe between the turbo compressor and the charge air cooler. Squeezing the air heats it a lot; Cummins notes in patent US6401457 that excessive outlet temperature can melt the compressor housing or harm the wheel, and still estimated the value in 2001 because no series sensor lasted there.
s: Check engine lamp on
Compressor outlet temperature missing or jumping in live data
Boost limitation at high load possibly less refined
c: Loose or corroded connector on the charge pipe sensor
Wire breaking intermittently near the hot turbocharger
Faulty input in the engine control module

P2EA7.d: A DC/AC converter turns direct current into household AC for sockets in the vehicle. P2EA7 means the DC voltage reaching converter A is below the range in which it is allowed to run.
s: AC sockets in the vehicle deliver no power or cut out
Message about the power outlet or inverter in the cluster
Problem appears mainly with engine off or at low battery charge
c: Weak, discharged or aged 12 V battery
Voltage drop at the supply fuse, cable or ground point of the converter
Hybrid high-voltage supply restricted, for example at very low state of charge
Faulty input voltage measurement inside the converter

P2EA8.d: P2EA8 is the reverse of P2EA7: the DC input of converter A lies above its permitted window. In the 12 V design of Toyota Industries' patent US10050558 the inverter stops once the battery side exceeds about 16 V, for example after a jump start from a 24 V source or with a failed alternator regulator.
s: AC sockets switch off and stay off until a restart
Other overvoltage messages or flickering lights
c: Charging system overvoltage from a faulty alternator regulator or DC/DC converter
Jump start or charging with too high a voltage
Faulty input voltage measurement inside the converter

P2EA9.d: P2EA9 reports that converter A has become too hot. The converter watches the power devices that switch and invert the current – MOSFETs, diodes and transistors – and in Toyota Industries' patent US10050558 it stops once their temperature passes a set limit, then waits for a manual reset, the same handling as an input overvoltage.
s: AC sockets switch off under load
Output only returns after cooling and a restart
c: Long operation near the rated power
Cooling air path blocked or cooling fan failed
High temperature at the mounting location
Faulty temperature sensing or power stage in the converter

P2EAA.d: The active radiator air flow system meters cooling air with motor-driven flaps between bumper opening and radiator; J2012 keeps its control module apart from the grille shutter modules (P05C0, U0284). Hyundai and Kia's patent US11225900 shows such a system with two flap zones, each moved by its own actuator according to vehicle speed, outside and coolant temperature and refrigerant pressure.
s: Check engine lamp on, where the maker assigns a MIL
Flaps stay in one position
Slower warm-up or slightly higher fuel consumption
c: Corroded or loose connector in the exposed front-end area
Supply or ground of the module outside its range
Internal fault in control module A

P2EAB.d: P2EAB means module A of the active radiator air flow system reports that its own electronics have overheated. Such smart actuators carry their motor driver on board and protect it: J2012 records the matching case for the grille shutter as P05C0, where the actuator switches its output stage off when the chip runs too hot.
s: Check engine lamp on, where the maker assigns a MIL
Flaps stop moving for a while
Higher coolant temperature under load if the flaps are stuck closed
c: Flaps blocked by ice, dirt or a damaged linkage, motor overloaded
High heat at the mounting place near the radiator
Internal fault in the module or its temperature sensing

P2EAC.d: P2EAC is the general performance fault of module A: the module can be reached, but the flap system does not do what it is told. GM's check of the comparable smart shutter actuator on the 3.0 L diesel LZ0 shows the approach: a gap of more than 5 % between commanded and reported position starts repeated attempts to free the flaps, and only after a calibrated number of failed retries is the fault confirmed, type B with
s: Check engine lamp on, where the maker assigns a MIL
Flaps do not open or close, sometimes only in frost
Warmer engine under load or slower warm-up
c: Flaps frozen or blocked by debris
Worn gearbox or motor in the actuator

P2EAD.d: Some diesels dose DEF at two points, each with its own metering unit or injector. P2EAD means the second one no longer delivers what it should.
s: Check engine lamp on
DEF warning and, if not repaired, speed limitation
Higher NOx emissions
c: Second DEF injector crusted or partly blocked by urea crystals
Kinked, frozen or blocked line to the second injector
Engine control software needing an update (GM LZ0 2023)
Weak DEF pump or pressure sensor deviation

P2EAE.d: P2EAE concerns the second DEF injector on bank 1. Open, low and high circuit faults have their own codes, P2053 to P2055; here the circuit works, yet its signal does not fit a properly moving valve.
s: Check engine lamp on
DEF system warning
Higher NOx emissions
c: Armature of the second injector sticking from urea crystals
Corroded contacts distorting the current trace

P2EAF.d: P2EAF means the second DEF injector on bank 1 stays shut although it is commanded open, so the SCR stage it serves gets no reductant. It is the unit 2 counterpart of P208E.
s: Check engine lamp on
DEF warning with countdown to speed limitation
Higher NOx emissions
c: Corrosion inside the injector after poor fluid or long standstill
Blocked or frozen supply line to the second injector

P2EB0.d: P2EB0 concerns the sensor that measures air pressure at the inlet of the throttle valve, i.e. between charger or air filter and throttle.
s: Check engine lamp on
Reduced boost or hesitant acceleration if a substitute value is used
Other air system checks such as the PCV monitor may not run
c: Loose, corroded or oil-wetted connector at the sensor
Intermittent break in signal, reference or ground wire
Failed sensor electronics, e.g. SENT output

P2EB1.d: P2EB1 says the pressure signal at the throttle inlet is below the lowest valid voltage. These sensors are linear: Ford's transfer curve gives about 0.4 V at 20 kPa and 4.5 V at 300 kPa, so a low voltage reads as an absurdly low pressure.
s: Check engine lamp, often after the first trip
Noticeable loss of power under load
Pressure reading far below ambient in live data
c: 5 V reference open or shorted, often shared with other sensors

P2EB2.d: P2EB2 is stored when the throttle inlet pressure signal exceeds its upper limit. Since voltage climbs with pressure, the module would read a boost no charger can deliver.
s: Check engine lamp, often after the first trip
Boost limited, sluggish response
Pressure reading far above ambient with the engine off
c: Open sensor ground or corroded ground pin
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2EB3.d: P2EB3 covers a throttle inlet pressure that is electrically fine but wrong. With the engine stopped, the pressure ahead of the throttle must equal manifold and barometric pressure; Ford checks this at key-up after at least 10 s off, allowing about 2.7 inHg between boost and manifold sensor.
s: Check engine lamp on
Pressure reading differs from manifold and barometric pressure with engine off
Uneven boost or reduced power
c: Sensor offset or drift with age
Pressure port blocked by oil residue or ice
Leak in the charge air path upsetting the model comparison

P2EB4.d: With inductive charging, the vehicle coil picks up high-frequency power from a ground pad and an on-board rectifier turns it into DC for the traction battery; SAE J2954 defines classes up to 11 kW around 85 kHz. Because this path carries high voltage, its plugs and covers sit in a high voltage interlock loop, a low-voltage signal wire that breaks as soon as a connector is pulled or a lid removed.
s: Inductive charging does not start or stops
Charging fault message
c: HV connector or cover of the charger not fully latched
Fault in the interlock evaluation of the module

P2EB5.d: P2EB5 reports that the input of the inductive charger receives too little voltage during power transfer. That input is the AC the vehicle coil collects from the ground pad across the air gap, so the level depends on alignment, gap and the power sent by the ground side.
s: Inductive charging slow or interrupted
Charging fault message
c: Vehicle not parked accurately over the ground pad
Object or ice between ground pad and vehicle coil
Ground unit delivering too little power
Faulty input voltage measurement in the charger

P2EB6.d: P2EB6 is the counterpart to P2EB5: the voltage at the input of the inductive charger is higher than its electronics accept. Too much induced voltage can stem from a ground unit sending more power than requested, a ride height that shifts the coupling, for example when the vehicle is loaded or unloaded during charging, or a control loop between both sides that has lost step.
s: Inductive charging stops shortly after starting
Charging fault message
c: Ground unit sending more power than requested
Coupling changed by ride height or position during charging
Disturbed communication between vehicle and ground unit
Faulty input voltage measurement in the charger

P2EB7.d: P2EB7 is a request rather than a classic fault: the vehicle considers its 12 V battery due for replacement. Energy management judges battery condition through a sensor or a battery with its own electronics on the LIN bus; HELLA's intelligent battery sensor, for example, measures voltage, current and temperature and works out state of charge, health and function.
s: Code stored without warning lamp
Possibly weak starting or reduced start-stop operation
c: 12 V battery worn, low remaining capacity
Brief LIN communication fault with the battery module (Bentley 2025)
New battery fitted but not registered or of the wrong type

P2EB9.d: P2EB9 is the bank 2 twin of P2EAE: the circuit of the second DEF injector on the second exhaust bank works electrically, but its signal does not match a valve that opens and closes as it should. Bank 2 implies a separate exhaust line for the second cylinder bank, and unit 2 a further dosing point on that line.
s: Check engine lamp on
DEF system warning
Higher NOx emissions
c: Corroded contacts distorting the current trace

P2EBB.d: P2EBB is the general circuit fault of a sensor that reports the temperature inside the crankcase, i.e. of the blow-by gas or the space above the oil.
s: Check engine lamp on
Crankcase temperature missing or jumping in live data
No noticeable change in how the engine runs
c: Connector loose or contaminated with engine oil
Harness wire breaking intermittently on the engine block

P2EBC.d: P2EBC means the crankcase temperature sensor delivers an electrically valid value that does not suit the engine state: it may stick, react too slowly or sit far from the coolant and oil temperatures after a long stop. The CARB rule 13 CCR 1968.2 calls in (e)(15.2.1) for rationality checks that catch readings that are wrongly high as well as wrongly low.
s: Check engine lamp after the fault is confirmed
Crankcase reading disagrees with oil and coolant temperature on a cold start
Crankcase ventilation checks may not complete
c: Sensor drifted or slow because of sludge or oil coking on the tip
Contact resistance in the connector shifting the value
Replacement sensor with a different characteristic fitted

P2EBD.d: P2EBD is set when the crankcase temperature signal rises above its highest valid voltage. With the usual pull-up arrangement this happens when the current path through the sensor is interrupted, for example by an unplugged or oil-soaked connector, a broken wire or an open element, or when the signal touches the 5 V reference or battery voltage.
s: Check engine lamp on
Crankcase temperature fixed at an extreme value
Engine runs normally
c: Connector unplugged, oil-soaked or with spread terminals
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2EBE.d: P2EBE reports a crankcase temperature signal below the lowest voltage the circuit can produce when intact. In practice a short is behind it: either the signal lead has rubbed through to ground on the engine block, or the insulation inside the sensor has given way, for instance after oil has crept into the housing.
s: Check engine lamp on
Live data shows an implausible crankcase temperature
Crankcase heating or ventilation checks suspended
c: Signal wire chafed through to ground on the engine
Sensor shorted internally after oil ingress
Faulty input stage in the engine control module

P2EBF.d: P2EBF reports that the control used to select a battery charging mode stays in one state, most likely a button that reads as permanently pressed. On plug-in hybrids such a control makes the engine recharge the traction battery while driving: Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV had a separate Battery Charge (CHRG) switch that runs the engine until about 80 percent state of charge, and the 2026 model reaches the same mode thro
s: Engine keeps running to charge the traction battery
Charging mode cannot be switched on or off
Higher fuel use and less electric driving
c: Button mechanically jammed or contact welded in the pressed state
Spilled liquid or dirt in the console switch panel
Short in the switch signal wire imitating a held button

P2EC0.d: P2EC0 reports that the compressor outlet temperature signal has fallen under the lowest valid voltage. Air temperature sensors on the intake side are usually NTC thermistors, as Bosch states for its combined boost pressure and temperature sensor; their resistance shrinks as they warm, so a signal pulled towards ground is read as extreme heat.
s: Check engine lamp on
Live data shows an implausibly hot charge air temperature
Possible loss of power if a substitute value limits boost
c: Signal wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed on the charge pipe
Oil or moisture bridging the connector pins

P2EC1.d: P2EC1 is set when the compressor outlet temperature sensor delivers a voltage above its permitted window. Because the module feeds the sensor through a pull-up resistor, any break in the current path lifts the input to the reference: an unplugged or corroded connector, a cracked wire or a burnt-out element.
s: Check engine lamp on
Live data shows a fixed extreme value
Usually no noticeable change in driving
c: Connector unplugged, corroded or with spread terminals
Signal shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2EC2.d: P2EC2 flags a compressor outlet temperature that is electrically valid but does not fit the operating point. A reference is easy to build: Cummins (US6401457) derives the outlet temperature from inlet temperature and pressure, turbo speed, air mass and pressure ratio, and after a long soak the sensor should also agree with intake and ambient readings.
s: Check engine lamp after the fault is confirmed
Reading disagrees with intake and ambient temperature after a cold soak
Charge air cooler diagnosis may be suspended
c: Sensor drifted or reacting too slowly
Tip coated with oil from crankcase or turbo seals
Sensor loose or not reaching into the air stream
